name: BSc Agriculture
title: BSc Agriculture
intro: The agriculture roadmap: ICAR/CUET admission, four years of study, practical RAWE training and careers in agri-business and government.

phases.title: Class 11–12 subjects
phases.summary: Science with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (or Maths/Agriculture) is the usual requirement.
points: Most agricultural universities need Class 12 PCB, PCM or PCMB; some accept Agriculture as a vocational stream.
Build biology and chemistry basics and learn about crops, soils and weather.
Visit farms, agricultural fairs and Krishi Vigyan Kendras to understand the field.
Check minimum marks and age limits for the universities you want.

phases.title: Entrance exams and admission
phases.summary: ICAR-affiliated seats are filled through CUET-UG; state agricultural universities use state CETs and merit.
points: For ICAR-affiliated universities, register for CUET-UG with the required science subjects and take part in counselling.
State agricultural universities run their own entrances or use state CET scores with counselling.
ICAR reserves 15% of seats in participating universities for All India Quota candidates.
Compare farms, labs and RAWE tie-ups before choosing a university.

phases.title: Year 1: foundation papers
phases.summary: Core science papers and lab skills.
points: Core papers: Fundamentals of Agronomy, Soil Science, Plant Biochemistry, Genetics and Rural Sociology.
Under NEP you also take language, environment and skill-enhancement courses.
Learn to maintain a lab notebook, follow safety rules and write practical reports.
Start reading beyond the syllabus and attend department seminars.

phases.title: Year 2–3: advanced and applied papers
phases.summary: Deeper papers, electives and a project.
points: Year 2: Crop Production, Plant Pathology, Entomology, Agricultural Economics and Horticulture.
Year 3: Agri-business Management, Farm Machinery, Post-harvest Technology, Extension Education and electives, with Rural Agricultural Work Experience (RAWE) in the final year.
Complete a project or dissertation under a faculty guide.
Many universities offer a fourth Honours year with research.

phases.title: Lab skills, internships and training
points: Learn: soil and plant testing, farm machinery, crop planning, plant protection methods and GIS or farm-tech tools.
Do summer internships or short research projects in labs, companies and government institutions.
Take certificate courses on SWAYAM, NPTEL or industry bodies.
Keep a record of your projects, certificates and skills.

phases.title: After BSc: MSc, exams and careers
phases.summary: Master’s degree, NET/JRF, government jobs or industry.
points: Further study and careers: MSc Agriculture, MBA Agri-business, agri-extension officer, agri-input company roles, banking (agri officer) and food industry.
Exams: CUET-PG (ICAR), ICAR NET/ASRB, IBPS Agriculture Field Officer, state agriculture department exams and UPSC (Indian Forest Service).
Research route: MSc, then CSIR-UGC NET (JRF) or GATE and a PhD.
Government exams such as SSC and state PSCs are open to science graduates.
